 Sunderland fan set for emotional visit to his mother's homeland as team play in Poznan 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article Sunderland supporters are braced for another Europa Cup night, but for Chris Henry it carries extra meaning. The 44-year-old is travelling to Poland, his mother's homeland, for the tie at Lech Poznan's Poznan Stadium.
 According to Sunderland Echo, Henry follows the Black Cats across the UK as part of the South Shields and Washington Sunderland Supporters branch. This fixture stands out for him given his family roots.
 OneFootball Videos
 His mother, Gosha, left Poland for Sunderland in 1981 after meeting his dad, Billy, a bricklayer working there in the late 1970s and early 1980s. Her hometown is Aleksandrow Kujawski, a small place of about 10,000 people, with Toruń the nearest big city.
 Henry also offered a note to fellow fans in Polish, which he said translates as Haway the Lads.
 Fellow supporter Peter Oliver has shared photos from a 4,500 mile journey as he bids to follow the team he loves.
 Source: Sunderland Echo
